recent_posts.title: What senior engineers at big tech actually spend their time doing
recent_posts.summary: At companies like Google, Amazon, and Netflix, senior engineers often spend weeks or months writing design docs and RFCs before any code is written — and sometimes go months without touching production code. Their value lies in architectural thinking and system design, not raw output. The rise of AI hasn't changed this principle; it has only amplified the importance of clear thinking and intentional design over typing speed.

React Native Full Course 2026 | Build, Publish and Monetize a Full Stack Mobile App to App Store
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive full-course walkthrough for building, publishing, and monetizing a full-stack mobile app using React Native and Expo. Covers React Native fundamentals (components, styling, routing), setting up Expo with file-based routing via Expo Router, styling with NativeWind (Tailwind CSS for React Native), authentication and billing with Clerk, analytics with PostHog, AI code reviews with CodeRabbit, and deploying to both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store via EAS. The project built is 'Recurly', a subscription management app backed by Node.js, Express, and MongoDB.

recent_posts.title: How to vibe code a complex 3D product website using a 7-step AI workflow
recent_posts.summary: A developer built a high-end 3D basketball e-commerce website solo using AI (Gemini/Google AI Studio), React 19, Three.js via React Three Fiber, and GSAP scroll animations. The post outlines a 7-step workflow for agentic development: research references first, define goals before prompting, build a structured master prompt, iterate surgically with specific feedback, tackle one problem at a time, understand the code you ship, and build in public. The project featured procedural leather textures, Web Audio API sound effects, and a complex 3D-to-2D cart animation — all under 3MB. The author also promotes a SaaS tool for generating master prompts and an upcoming AI development course.

recent_posts.title: Build and Deploy a Full Stack AI Voice Learning App
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive tutorial for building a full-stack AI voice learning app called 'Bookify' where users upload PDFs and have voice conversations with the content. The stack includes Next.js, MongoDB, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript, Clerk for auth/subscriptions, Vapi for real-time voice, and shadcn/ui for components. The tutorial covers project setup, navbar, authentication with Clerk, homepage UI, book upload form with React Hook Form and Zod validation, MongoDB database setup, and GitHub workflow with CodeRabbit for AI-powered PR reviews. The JetBrains AI agent Junie is used throughout to accelerate development. The app is designed to be monetized as a SaaS with subscription tiers.

recent_posts.title: OpenClaw Full Course | Set Up and Deploy Your Own AI Agent
recent_posts.summary: A full walkthrough on setting up and deploying OpenClaw, an AI agent orchestration layer that connects LLMs (Claude, GPT, Gemini) to a VPS and messaging apps like Telegram. The guide covers deploying on a Hostinger VPS using a one-click template, configuring a Telegram bot, customizing the agent's personality via a soul.md file, and five real developer workflows: deploying code from a phone via Vercel, managing GitHub PRs and email from Telegram, running deep research on a schedule, building persistent memory, and creating custom skills through natural language. Advanced tips include memory management, multi-model switching, voice message support, and multi-agent setups.

recent_posts.title: Build an AI floor plan visualizer with React and serverless backend
recent_posts.summary: Step-by-step tutorial building Roomifi, an AI-powered architectural visualization SaaS that converts 2D floor plans into photorealistic 3D renders. Uses React, Vite, React Router v7, and Puter.js for serverless backend, AI models, and file hosting—all without credit cards or API keys. Covers authentication, drag-and-drop upload, progress tracking, routing, and AI code generation with JetBrains Juny and CodeRabbit for reviews. Implements user-pays model where infrastructure costs scale with users, not developers.
